verses.text: Elihu went on:
Bear with me a little longer and I’ll explain. I still have something to say on God’s behalf.
I’ll draw on knowledge from far away and show that my Maker does what is right.
What I’m telling you is true. Someone with complete knowledge is here with you.
Look, God is mighty, yet he looks down on no one. His understanding is as great as his strength.
He doesn’t keep the wicked alive, but he gives justice to those who suffer.
He keeps his eyes on the righteous. He seats them with kings on their thrones and lifts them up forever.
If they are bound in chains and caught in the ropes of suffering,
he shows them what they’ve done wrong and how proudly they’ve acted.
He opens their ears to correction and tells them to turn away from wrongdoing.
If they listen and serve him, they’ll live out their days in prosperity and their years in joy.
But if they refuse to listen, they’ll die by the sword without ever understanding.
People whose hearts turn away from God store up anger. They don’t cry for help when he binds them.
They die young, and their lives end among the unclean.
God rescues suffering people through their suffering. He gets their attention in the middle of their oppression.
He would have drawn you out of trouble into a wide-open place where nothing could hem you in. Your table would have been loaded with rich food.
But now you’re weighed down with the judgment that falls on the wicked. Judgment and justice have taken hold of you.
Watch out that wealth doesn’t lure you into anger or a big bribe turn you aside.
Could your wealth or all your strength keep you going when trouble comes?
Don’t long for the night, when people are cut off where they stand.
Be careful to stay away from wrongdoing. You’ve chosen it over suffering.
God is exalted in his power. Who teaches like he does?
Who has told him what to do? Who can say to him, ‘You’ve done wrong’?
Remember to praise what he’s done, the work people have sung about.
Everyone has looked at it. People can see it from far away.
God is great beyond what we can know. No one can count his years.
He draws up drops of water, and the vapor condenses into rain.
The clouds pour it out, and it falls on people in abundance.
Can anyone understand how the clouds spread or how thunder rolls from his shelter?
Look how he spreads his light all around him. He covers the depths of the sea.
By these things he judges the peoples and gives them plenty of food.
He fills his hands with lightning and tells it where to strike.
The thunder announces him, and the cattle sense the storm coming.
